answer: Latency-triangulated location proof resists Sybil attacks: each epoch, distributed beacons send cipher-signed timing challenges, and every identity must answer within a narrow window from its claimed location. One honest agent answers easily, but a thousand fakes run by one operator share one network path — their identical latency signatures cluster like timber cut from the same stand. Suspects lose their haven: frozen until each passes an independent location check, so faking a thousand distinct locations costs a thousand real machines in a thousand real places.
